title: CSS Grid
canDo: build two-dimensional layouts with CSS Grid

sources.name: Kevin Powell — Learn CSS Grid the easy way

blocks.md: Flexbox is great for one direction (a row *or* a column). Grid is for two directions at once — rows **and** columns — like a real page layout or a calendar of days.

blocks.canDo: build two-dimensional layouts with CSS Grid

blocks.md:
**What to focus on:**

- `display: grid` turns a container into a grid.
- `grid-template-columns` defines the columns — `repeat(3, 1fr)` makes 3 equal columns (`fr` = a fraction of free space).
- `gap` — space between cells.
- Spanning cells across multiple columns/rows.

Use Flexbox when content flows in one line; reach for Grid when you're placing things into a real 2-D structure.

blocks.title: Learn CSS Grid the easy way
blocks.note: ~37 min. Same teacher, same clear style — follow along in your own editor.

blocks.label: 🥕 Play all 28 levels of Grid Garden to drill cell *placement* (line numbers and spanning). Note: the game focuses on placement — `fr` units and `gap` come from the video above, not the game. ~30 min.

questions.question: What does `grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr)` produce?
options: Three columns where the first takes up 3 times the space of the others
Three equal-width columns that share the available space
Three columns each exactly 1 pixel wide
questions.explanation: `1fr` is one fraction of the free space, so `repeat(3, 1fr)` creates three columns that each receive an equal share of the container width.

questions.question: Which CSS property do you use to control the space between grid cells (rows and columns)?
questions.explanation: The `gap` property (formerly `grid-gap`) sets the gutter between rows and columns in a grid container.

questions.question: A grid item needs to span across two columns. Which declaration achieves that?
questions.explanation: `grid-column: span 2` tells the item to occupy two consecutive column tracks from wherever it is placed.
